newsitem.title: LEBANON: Princeton professor chosen to head Beirut's AUB university.
newsitem.headline: Princeton professor chosen to head Beirut's AUB university.

text.p: John Waterbury, a professor at Princeton University in the United States, has been appointed president of the American University of Beirut (AUB), a university statement announced on Monday.
Waterbury, a former director of Princeton's Center of International Studies, is currently professor of politics and international affairs, the statement said.
AUB, founded in 1866, is one of the Arab world's most prestigious universities and has a student body of some 5,000. Waterbury succeeds David Dodge who has served as acting president since 1996.
It was not clear from the AUB statement if Waterbury would reside in Lebanon.
Americans are not allowed to live in Lebanon because of a ban by Washington on travel by U.S. citizens to Beirut that dates to the 1975-90 civil war.
The university's palm-studded seaside campus was a target of Moslem militants waging an anti-Western campaign of bombings, assassinations and kidnappings during the civil war.
One AUB president and several Western faculty members were killed or kidnapped by Moslem militants.
In 1984, AUB president Malcolm Kerr was killed by gunmen as he was entering his office.
Less than two years earlier, Kerr's predecessor David Dodge, also an American, was kidnapped on campus and later freed after being held in Iran.
